correctness.rationale: Each facet has area sqrt(3)/2 and normal proportional to −(e_i−1/4·1); summing the absolute projected facet areas and dividing by two gives A=||u||_1/2 in the stated edge-length units. An independent formulation uses the orthonormal columns (1,1,−1,−1)/2, (1,−1,1,−1)/2, (1,−1,−1,1)/2 as coordinates x in the tangent hyperplane. The maximizing orbit is the signed coordinate axes, so chord distance squared is 2(1−M) where M=||x||_infinity. Sorting absolute values and summing the four signed linear forms gives A=max(M,||x||_1/2). On the M branch, away from the axes, the stability quotient is exactly 1/2. On the other branch put B=||x||_1/2; M≥2B/3 and B≤sqrt(3)/2 give quotient at least (1−B)/(2(1−2B/3)), decreasing strictly in B. At its minimum B=sqrt(3)/2 both bounds are attained and force |x_i|=1/sqrt(3), giving exactly the eight vertex axes in the original coordinates. At the maximizing axes both sides are zero; the branch interface causes no additional equality. The exact witness evaluates to (3−sqrt(3))/8, so the lower bound is globally sharp.
residual_risks: The finite symbolic witness alone would not establish the global bound; the two-branch argument supplies it.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the best global coefficient and its full equality set, not the previously known area function, maximizing orbit, or optimal quadratic exponent. The strongest same-setting stability theorem has coefficient 1/10 in the same normalization, strictly below (3−sqrt(3))/8. Same-body shadow distribution and chamber formulas supply inputs but no pointwise optimal distance-deficit tradeoff. An indexed same-form sharp theorem on a 5D cross-polytope has neither the same body nor an identified reduction that yields this coefficient.
residual_risks: Historical scan not independently read; an indexed-by-other-terminology norm inequality could still supply the same tradeoff. No inference of chronological priority is made from same-day dates.

value.rationale: This resolves the exact global coefficient for the first nonplanar regular simplex, a specified case of an existing quantitative projection theorem. Its sharp obstruction is qualitatively useful: the local coefficient near the maximizing square-shadow directions is 1/2, whereas the true bound is smaller and is forced by vertex-axis triangular shadows. This is a complete sharpness and equality result, not a tiny numeric improvement or a finite sampling exercise.
residual_risks: No extension asserted for other tetrahedra or higher-dimensional simplex projections.
